findings.claim: The panel-format declaration is a single global key (protocol["data"]["panel_format"]), but the E5 protocol the caller will use is one file spanning three markets (draft keys: markets = {IDX, CRYPTO, US}) that need three different formats (IDX panel-v2, US panel-global-v2-units, CRYPTO panel-global-v1). One declaration cannot satisfy all three, so e5.py cannot construct the IDX and US studies from the same frozen protocol file.
findings.evidence: Probe (PYTHONPATH=. python3 review_probe.py): a copy of the E1 protocol with data.panel_format = "panel-global-v2-units" run on the IDX jumpy_panel (format panel-v2) raises `ValueError: KOD-IDX-E1-v1 needs a panel-global-v2-units panel`. E5_CEILING_protocol_draft.json has top-level `markets` with IDX/CRYPTO/US and no per-market `data` block; the pinned panels on disk are panel-20261013T194245Z (panel-v2), panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z (panel-global-v2-units), panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z (panel-global-v1). The builder's own needs_other_file note ('use a protocol whose data.panel_format names panel-global-v2-units') would force per-market protocol files, so the recorded protocol_sha256 would differ per market or not be the frozen protocol's.
findings.fix: Additive, in e1.py only: resolve a per-market declaration first, e.g. `mk = (proto.get("markets") or {}).get(self.profile.market); declared = (mk.get("panel_format") if isinstance(mk, dict) else None) or (proto.get("data") or {}).get("panel_format")`, and/or add a `panel_format: str | None = None` keyword to Study that overrides the protocol's declaration (validated against PANEL_FORMATS). Keep the existing global-key behaviour. Add a test that one protocol declaring markets.IDX.panel_format=panel-v2 and markets.US.panel_format=panel-global-v2-units constructs both an IDX study (jumpy_panel) and a US study (us_panel) and still refuses a mismatched panel. Defaults are unaffected (E1's protocol has no markets block; E2's markets entries carry no panel_format).

findings.claim: unit_factor is attached to the Market whenever the column exists, not only under pool_units="as_traded"; Market.with_units requires every value finite and > 0, so a panel whose unit_factor column contains NaN now fails at Study construction even on the default path.
findings.evidence: Probe 2: us_panel with three unit_factor cells set to NaN, default pool_units, raises `ValueError: unit_factor must be finite, positive and shaped like the market`. No recorded run is affected (E1/E2 panels have no unit_factor column; the repair panels' factors are all finite, as backtest.run's with_units on them shows), and the builder disclosed it, but it is a default-path failure mode that did not exist at ae2cbee.
findings.fix: Attach only when pool_units == "as_traded" (the task wording), or keep the attach but guard it: attach when the column is present AND all finite/positive, else only raise under pool_units="as_traded". Add one test: a NaN in unit_factor under defaults constructs; under as_traded raises.

findings.claim: PANEL_FORMATS omits "panel-global-v2", which is global_panel.FORMAT (the current non-repair global build) and the format of panel_crypto-20261013T205803Z on disk; a protocol declaring it is refused.
findings.evidence: Probe 4: protocol_with("panel-global-v2") raises `ValueError: KOD-GLOBAL-E2-v1 names panel format 'panel-global-v2'; known: ('panel-v2', 'panel-global-v1', 'panel-global-v2-units')`. Manifest listing: panel_crypto-20261013T205803Z.json format panel-global-v2. The E5 draft pins the older crypto panel (panel-global-v1), so this bites only if E5 switches to the rebuilt crypto panel; the builder disclosed it.
findings.fix: Add "panel-global-v2" to PANEL_FORMATS (reachable only by explicit declaration, so still opt-in) and extend test_unknown_declared_formats_are_refused's tuple assertion.

findings.claim: test_evaluate_runs_under_v3 asserts only that volatility_q appears in last_flags and relaxed steps are within 0..4; it would pass if evaluate's pooling ignored the volatility key (coverage of the key comes only from the matched_controls test via the shared _pool).
findings.evidence: The test body checks `assertIn("volatility_q", st.last_flags.columns)` and the range of `matched_random_relaxed_steps` keys; neither depends on the draws sharing the volatility bucket.
findings.fix: After evaluate, recompute `_pool(n, d, elig)` for a few flagged cells with relaxed 0 and assert the pool's volatility bucket equals the flag's (or expose the draws and assert `buckets["volatility"][draws, d] == buckets["volatility"][n, d]` where relaxed == 0).
